approach: Add crates/athena-core/src/preflight.rs. It works out the tools a job needs: `git`, plus each capability check's program when that program is a bare name. It looks each tool up on PATH through an injectable `ToolProbe` (the system probe scans PATH entries for an executable file and runs nothing). It returns a `Preflight` with every tool checked, the blockers (tool, which checks need it, non-empty workaround steps), a one-line-per-tool note, and a stop reason. `Athena::dispatch` (run/mod.rs) calls it after `capability.checks(&jc)`. It stores the note in the existing `Job.note`, committed in the prediction commit before any agent runs. A blocker closes the job through `close_dispatched` as `failed` with an `environment: preflight blocked: ...` reason, before the resume, planning and producer branches. If the job was resuming kept work, the stop leaves that work alone and the reason names the earlier job to retry. `scope_guard::resumed_candidate` ignores a preflight-stopped job. The three dispatch tests go in run/tests.rs, next to the harness they use. The spec entry and the CHANGELOG line are then filled in. The spec mechanism says exactly what is probed: git and the check programs. `gh` and the agent binary are left out on purpose (decision 1).

decisions.choice: Needed tools are `git` plus the first element of each check's `run` when it is a bare name (non-empty, no `/`). Each tool is listed once, with the names of the checks that need it. `gh` and the agent binary are deliberately not probed (finding 1, option b). The spec mechanism says 'git and the bare-name check programs of the capability' and states that gh and the agent binary are not probed.
decisions.reason: The job run does not fail on a missing gh. `early_pr` turns any failure into one warning line and never changes the outcome (gh/early.rs:425-437). `push_ci_branch` and `delete_ci_branch` use git and only warn (early.rs:393-399, 414-418). `GhCli` (gh/transport.rs:23) is needed by `athena land` and the PR host calls, a separate command run after the job closes. Probing gh at dispatch would refuse jobs that finish today, contradicting criterion 5 (0% newly refused). The agent binary belongs to the athena-agent driver, which is not a deliverable and is a trait object that tests replace with a fake. Checks run with the process PATH (`env_pass` includes PATH, athena.toml:52; `Command::new` resolves through it, checks.rs:532-536), so check programs are a true need. A check named by a path (lifecycle.rs:129-152 uses `/nonexistent/athena-baseline-check` and must still land) is not looked up on PATH, so it is not a need. A unit test pins that gh is not a need, so the choice is visible.

rejected.option: Add gh when `gh::parse_remote` accepts the origin, with a cfg(any(test, feature="test-support")) probe seam for the CLI tests
rejected.why: The job does not need gh to run (early.rs:425-437 only warns). It would refuse jobs on a GitHub origin that finish today. It also needs a new feature-gated seam reachable from athena-cli and changes outside the deliverables.

rejected.option: Probe every check program, paths included
rejected.why: It would fail the lifecycle test that must still land (lifecycle.rs:129-152).
It misses what a capability's checks actually run and ignores per-capability needs.

rejected.option: A `required_tools()` method on the Capability trait
rejected.why: It needs overrides in athena-cap-change and athena-cap-study, which are not deliverables. The checks already name the programs (capability.rs:117).

decisions.choice: `SystemProbe` answers 'is the bare name an executable file in a PATH entry' by scanning the PATH variable (`std::env::split_paths`). An empty entry is skipped. A candidate counts when `std::fs::metadata` says it is a file with any execute bit set (unix; on other targets, a file). It runs nothing. The type is `SystemProbe { path: Option<OsString> }` with `from_env()` and `with_path(..)`, so tests give it a temp directory instead of changing the environment. The trait is one method, `present(&self, tool: &str) -> bool`.
decisions.reason: Finding 4. `Command::new` finds a program by this same PATH lookup. Running `<tool> --version` would run whatever script athena.toml names, with side effects. A hanging tool would add seconds to every dispatch, and killing only the direct child leaves its children running (athena-agent kills whole process groups elsewhere). A PATH scan costs nothing and has no side effects. This replaces the `--version` run assumed in the accepted reading. The reading's real aim, a probe that can be injected so a test can simulate a missing tool, is kept. A plan step and a risk note the change.

rejected.why: It has side effects for scripts that ignore `--version`, can add up to 5 s per tool, and leaves grandchildren running unless a process group is set up.

rejected.option: Run `--version` in its own process group with a short wait
rejected.why: More code (process group setup, kill, wait) to answer a question PATH lookup answers without running anything.

decisions.choice: No test seam and no new field on Athena. The pure function `preflight(&[Need], &dyn ToolProbe)` takes the probe as an argument, and unit tests pass a `FakeProbe`. `check_tools(capability_id, &[CheckSpec])` is the production entry; it builds `SystemProbe::from_env()`. The dispatch-level tests use the real probe: the missing case gives the test capability a check program `athena-preflight-absent-tool`, which is on no PATH; the present case uses `true`, which is.
decisions.reason: `Athena` is built by struct literal in about 67 places across 41 files (lib.rs:218 `pinner` shows the field style), so a field would touch files far outside the deliverables. A per-thread cfg(test) seam is no longer needed once gh is not probed and the dispatch tests can name an absent check program.

rejected.option: A `tool_probe: Box<dyn ToolProbe>` field on Athena
rejected.why: It breaks every struct literal in 41 files.

rejected.option: A per-thread cfg(test) seam modelled on run::check_seam
rejected.why: Extra moving parts. The real probe plus an absent program name shows the same thing.

decisions.choice: Record the preflight in the existing `Job.note` (Option<String>, athena-data/src/records.rs:625), set at the `Job` literal (run/mod.rs:1250, now `None`). It is committed in the prediction commit (run/mod.rs:1261) before any agent runs. The blocker and workaround are also in the closing outcome reason. No new record type, finding record, or file.
decisions.reason: Nothing reads `Job.note` today (searched crates for `job.note`, `record.note` and `.note` on Job: none). The prediction commit is made after the preflight and before the producer, so every probed tool is recorded, present or not. A job that stops before the producer has no candidate or plan, so a Blocker Finding in a Verification or Critique record has nowhere to live (records.rs:896-913, plan.rs:159-173).

rejected.why: It needs an AnyRecord variant, a canonical path, `check_record_file` and round-trip coverage in athena-data, and the brief allows no new record or data file.

rejected.option: A new Markdown file under the job directory
rejected.why: `check_record_file` allows only three names (records.rs:1411); athena-data is not a deliverable.
Both finding-bearing records need a candidate or a plan, which a job stopped before the producer does not have.

decisions.choice: The stop reason is `environment: preflight blocked: <tool> (needed by <checks>) is not on PATH; workaround: <steps>`. When the job was resuming earlier work, it ends with `; retry <earlier job> instead: its kept work was not used`. The job closes `failed` with `verification_passed = None`, as `stop_planning` does (planning.rs:8-14). The two lines are inlined in `dispatch`, so no helper is added.
decisions.reason: `StopCause::of` (disk.rs:450-463) classifies any `environment:` reason as `OtherEnvironment` with no change to disk.rs. The scope guard then does not count it as a failure of the work (scope_guard.rs:565-568), and drain ends its run only for ProducerAuth, LowDisk and UsageLimit. The helper is not put in pin.rs or preflight.rs (finding 7): `Closing` and `RunContext` are private to the `run` module (run/mod.rs:121, 1369) and `failure` is a private method (run/mod.rs:2470), so code outside `run` cannot name them. The body is two lines, so it sits inline in `dispatch`, and run/pin.rs stays unchanged.

rejected.why: It would count as a failure of the work and could raise the retry signal and pause the line.
It edits disk.rs and its tests, outside the deliverables; OtherEnvironment fits.
preflight.rs cannot reach the private types; pin.rs is for repository pinning and a two-line stop needs no helper.

decisions.choice: Keep earlier work when the preflight stops a retry that was resuming it (finding 2). `dispatch` computes `earlier` (the job id of `resume` (TimeoutSeed.job), or `resume_from` (ResumeSeed.job), including a stale merge) before the context is built. When a blocker exists, the context is built with `resume: None`, so `close_dispatched` does not call `remove_kept_work` (run/close.rs:152-154). The reason names the earlier job. The new job writes no resume mark and `closing.consumed_resume` stays `None`, so the earlier job's mark is untouched (`settle_resume_marks`, close.rs:155).
decisions.reason: A retry of the new, preflight-stopped job would look for its own mark and for a timeout state on itself (`resume_seed` reads the retried job's mark, run/mod.rs:542; `timeout_seed` checks the retried job's state, run/mod.rs:888-896), so it would plan and produce from scratch. Naming the earlier job in the reason sends the user to the job that still has the work. `athena retry <earlier>` then resumes it exactly as before.

rejected.option: Copy the earlier resume mark and kept directory to the new job id
rejected.why: It writes state files for a job that did no work and risks two marks for one candidate.

rejected.option: Run the preflight before the seeds are computed
rejected.why: It would stop the job with no record, so nothing records the blocker (no Job exists yet).

decisions.choice: Fix `scope_guard::resumed_candidate` (scope_guard.rs:621-627) to return false when the job's own outcome reason is a preflight stop (`preflight::is_preflight_reason`). This is finding 6, option 'have it require a non-preflight reason'.
decisions.reason: Without it, a retry that the preflight also stops meets all three conditions (a job record, no producer run, a resumable retried job) and its attempt is recorded `resumed = true` although nothing was resumed. The flag feeds `t3_basis`, which drops an environment attempt's spend when the next attempt resumed it (scope_guard.rs:296-305). The condition is one line, and a test covers it.

rejected.why: The flag is cheap to get right, and a mislabel would make the earlier preflight attempt's spend vanish from the line's T3 basis.

decisions.choice: Run the preflight in `dispatch` after the prediction-commit inputs exist and before the `resume_from` branch (run/mod.rs:1312). The probe itself runs just after `capability.checks(&jc)` (line 1153), before the Job literal, so the note is in the committed record.
decisions.reason: A blocker needs a Job to be recorded on. Resumed candidates still run the checks. Pre-dispatch bails (disk hold, `pin_repo` errors) leave no record and are unchanged.

rejected.why: It stops the job with no record.

decisions.reason: The change adds no parser, stem list, stop list or reading check. It reads no request or reading text. It refuses a job only when a program is absent from PATH. crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs concerns readings and is unaffected.

files.purpose: The module: `ToolProbe` trait (one method), `SystemProbe` (PATH scan, `from_env`/`with_path`), `Need { tool, needed_by }`, `Blocker { tool, needed_by, workaround }`, `Preflight { checked, blockers }` with `note()` and `stop_reason(earlier: Option<&JobId>)`, `needed_tools`, pure `preflight(&[Need], &dyn ToolProbe)`, production `check_tools`, `PREFLIGHT_BLOCKED` prefix and `is_preflight_reason`. Unit tests for criteria 1 and 2.
Add `pub mod preflight;` (after `pr_check`, before `proposals`) and a doc bullet in the module list.

In `dispatch`: compute `earlier`, call `crate::preflight::check_tools(capability.id(), &checks)` after line 1153, set `note: Some(tools.note())` at the Job literal (line 1250), build the context with `resume: None` when a blocker exists, and stop with `self.failure(..)` and `verification_passed = None` through `close_dispatched` before the `resume_from` branch (line 1312).
The three dispatch tests (A, B, C) next to the harness they use, named with `preflight` so `cargo test -p athena-core preflight` selects them.
`resumed_candidate` returns false when the job's own outcome reason is a preflight stop (one condition).

OLY-B-RUN-01 only (lines 2292-2296): mechanism naming preflight.rs and the run/mod.rs hook and saying what is and is not probed; keep `owner = "Athena"`; measure naming `cargo test -p athena-core preflight` that ends `status: not shown`.
One line under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added`: OLY-B-RUN-01 now has a mechanism, the capability preflight.

steps: Create crates/athena-core/src/preflight.rs with the types and functions listed in files. The workaround steps are always non-empty (install `<tool>` and put it on PATH, or change or remove the check that needs it in athena.toml, then run `athena retry <job>`), with a git-specific and a cargo-specific first step. `SystemProbe::present` scans the PATH entries (skip empty ones) for a file with an execute bit via `std::fs::metadata`, and runs nothing.

Add `pub const PREFLIGHT_BLOCKED: &str = "environment: preflight blocked:"` and `is_preflight_reason(&str) -> bool`. `stop_reason(&self, earlier: Option<&JobId>)` builds the reason from it and appends the earlier-job retry hint when `earlier` is given.
Add `pub mod preflight;` and a doc bullet to crates/athena-core/src/lib.rs.

Edit `dispatch` in crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs: (a) before line 1153 keep the seeds in hand and compute `earlier` from `resume` and `resume_from`; (b) after `capability.checks(&jc)` call `check_tools`; (c) set `note: Some(tools.note())` at the Job literal; (d) build the RunContext with `resume: if blocked.is_some() { None } else { resume }`; (e) before `if let Some(seed) = resume_from`, when a blocker exists, build `Closing::new()`, set `closing.happened = self.failure(&ctx, &reason)` and `closing.happened.verification_passed = None`, and `return self.close_dispatched(&ctx, closing)`. Leave run/pin.rs unchanged.

Write the unit tests in preflight.rs: `preflight_missing_tool_becomes_a_blocker_with_a_workaround_plan`, `preflight_all_tools_present_gives_no_blocker`, `preflight_skips_checks_named_by_path`, `preflight_shared_tool_listed_once`, `preflight_needs_come_from_the_capability_checks`, `preflight_gh_is_not_a_need`, `preflight_stop_reason_names_the_earlier_job`, `preflight_system_probe_finds_only_executable_files_on_path`, and `preflight_spec_entry_names_this_file_owner_and_test` (shaped like iris.rs:227-243, plus the `spec_gaps` assertion).
Write the three dispatch tests in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs (A, B, C) with the existing harness, as described in the criterion 3 demonstration.
Edit docs/spec.toml OLY-B-RUN-01 only: mechanism, `owner = "Athena"`, and a measure that contains `cargo test -p athena-core preflight` and ends with `status: not shown`. Then add the CHANGELOG line.

Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked` and `cargo test -p athena-core preflight`. Check that stubbing the body of `preflight()` makes the missing-tool test fail, and restore it.

risks.risk: The accepted reading assumed the probe runs `<tool> --version`; the plan looks the name up on PATH instead.
risks.mitigation: The injectable probe trait the reading asked for is kept. A PATH scan is what `Command::new` does and runs nothing (finding 4). The change is recorded in decision 2 and in the producer-visible plan steps, and the spec mechanism says 'on PATH'.

risks.risk: A host or test environment where a check's bare-name program is absent now stops the job with an environment reason instead of failing at the check.
risks.mitigation: This is the intended stricter behavior (criterion 5). The reason names the tool and gives a workaround. The programs in existing tests (git, sh, true, cargo) are on PATH, and path programs are skipped.

risks.risk: gh and the agent binary are not probed, so a job on a GitHub remote with no gh still fails later at landing (finding 1).
risks.mitigation: This is a deliberate scope choice with its reason (decision 1): a missing gh only produces a warning during the job. The spec mechanism states the limit instead of claiming every capability is checked. A unit test pins it.

risks.risk: The producer finds `run/pin.rs` listed in the brief's deliverables but the plan leaves it unchanged, and the unchanged-planned-files check sends the job back.
risks.mitigation: pin.rs is not in this plan's file list, because the stop is two inline lines and `Closing` and `RunContext` are private to `run`. If the check still fires, the report lists pin.rs under `unchanged_planned_files` with that reason.

risks.risk: The new `Job.note` makes job.json differ from fixtures of tests that compare whole records.
risks.mitigation: Searched the crates for whole-record comparisons of `note: None` on Job and found none. The athena-cli suites run under `cargo test --locked`, and a failure would show there.

risks.risk: Test C builds two Athena values over one state directory, which may behave differently from the single-instance tests.
risks.mitigation: `athena_with` already derives the state path from the given tempdir (tests.rs:198), and the existing resume tests retry through a fresh `retry`/`go`; the producer can fall back to one Athena with a capability whose check list the test changes through a shared cell if the second instance fails to see the first's records.

risks.risk: A retry of the preflight-stopped job itself starts from scratch because its own state has no kept work.
risks.mitigation: By design: the reason names the earlier job to retry (finding 2). Test C asserts the earlier job's work survives and `preflight_stop_reason_names_the_earlier_job` asserts the wording.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `preflight_spec_entry_names_this_file_owner_and_test` in preflight.rs, shaped like `iris_spec_entry_names_files_that_exist` (iris.rs:227-243). It parses the real spec with `crate::hestia::parse_spec(include_str!("../../../docs/spec.toml"))` and finds OLY-B-RUN-01. It asserts the entry is active, the owner is `Athena`, the mechanism contains `crates/athena-core/src/preflight.rs`, the measure contains the exact command `cargo test -p athena-core preflight` and ends with `status: not shown`, and `hestia::measure_problem(&measure)` is None. It also asserts `crate::hestia::spec_gaps(&requirements)` has no gap with id OLY-B-RUN-01, and that the file `crates/athena-core/src/preflight.rs` exists under the repository root (`env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")/../..`). The existing real-spec test in hestia.rs (4286) also runs.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core preflight_spec_entry && cargo test -p athena-core the_real_spec_records_every_field && git diff -- docs/spec.toml
demonstrations.observes: The tests pass. The diff shows OLY-B-RUN-01 (docs/spec.toml:2292-2296) changed from `mechanism = "none"` and the measure `The spec gap list; status: requirement` to a mechanism naming preflight.rs, run/mod.rs and 'git and the bare-name check programs; gh and the agent binary are not probed', `owner = "Athena"`, and a measure naming `cargo test -p athena-core preflight` that ends `status: not shown`. Only that requirement's lines change.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the spec entry unchanged, the mechanism is `none` and the measure is `...; status: requirement`. The existing hestia test and `measure_problem` already accept that measure (hestia.rs:4293, and `requirement` is a known label, status.rs:321), so they do not fail. The new test fails on its own assertions: the mechanism lacks the preflight.rs path, the measure lacks `cargo test -p athena-core preflight` and does not end with `status: not shown`, and `spec_gaps` still lists OLY-B-RUN-01 for its `none` mechanism. This corrects the earlier plan's claim that `measure_problem` would fail.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in preflight.rs call the production function `preflight::preflight(&needs, &probe)` and the production `needed_tools(capability_id, &checks)`. The fake is a small `FakeProbe { missing: Vec<&str> }` that only answers present or missing per tool name; it is passed as an argument. `preflight_missing_tool_becomes_a_blocker_with_a_workaround_plan`: checks `["cargo","fmt"]` and `["cargo","test"]`, FakeProbe missing `cargo`. It asserts exactly one blocker with tool `cargo`, needed_by listing both check names, at least one non-empty workaround step, a note with `git: present` and `cargo: missing`, and a `stop_reason(None)` that starts with `environment: preflight blocked:` and names `cargo` and a workaround. `preflight_all_tools_present_gives_no_blocker`: the same needs with nothing missing; it asserts no blockers, `stop_reason(None) == None`, and every needed tool in `checked` and in the note as present. demonstrations.observes: All tests whose name contains `preflight` pass, including the budget-reserve ones already in the crate and the dispatch tests of criterion 3. The missing-tool test shows one blocker naming `cargo` with a non-empty workaround; the all-present test shows none.

demonstrations.method: Three dispatch tests in run/tests.rs, using its existing harness (`repo()`, `athena_with(&repo, &state, check, plenty_of_space, script)`, `finished_job`, `counting`, `producer_ending`; Docs capability id `study`, run/tests.rs:90-215). They go through `Athena::go`, which reaches `dispatch`. Guards before the hook: `refuse_if_stopped`, the paused-line check (mod.rs:1026), the configuration-hash match (mod.rs:1030), `disk_gate` (tests use `plenty_of_space`), the budget reserve (mod.rs:1095) and `pin_repo` (not a pinning capability, so none). Test A, `preflight_blocks_a_missing_tool_before_the_producer_and_records_it`: `athena_with(.., &["athena-preflight-absent-tool"], .., counting(counts, None))`. It asserts state Failed, a reason that starts `environment: preflight blocked:` and names that tool and `workaround`, `is_environment_reason`, `StopCause::of == OtherEnvironment`, and `counts.all()` showing zero producer and zero verifier calls. It loads `Records` at `finished.prediction_commit` and asserts the Job `note` contains `git: present` and `athena-preflight-absent-tool: missing`, with no candidate yet. Test B, `preflight_records_every_probed_tool_when_all_are_present`: check `PASSES` (`true`). It asserts the producer ran once, the reason does not start with `environment:`, and the Job record loaded at `finished.prediction_commit` has a note with `git: present` and `true: present`; that commit predates any candidate, which shows the order. Test C, `preflight_stop_on_a_resumed_retry_keeps_the_earlier_work`: a first Athena with `producer_ending(Error, expired_login(), true, ..)` (the pattern at tests.rs:5316) closes failed with a login-expiry stop and keeps work in `state.root()/kept/<first>` (precondition asserted). A second Athena over the same state directory, with check `athena-preflight-absent-tool` and the `counting` script (it names the retried job in the reading, tests.rs:2527), runs `retry(first)` then `go`. It asserts the retry closes Failed with the environment preflight reason naming `first`, the kept directory still exists, `read_resume`/timeout seed for `first` is still found by `timeout_seed`, and `scope_guard::request_records(..)` shows the retry's attempt with `resumed == false` and verdict Environment.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core preflight_blocks_a_missing_tool preflight_records_every_probed_tool preflight_stop_on_a_resumed_retry && cargo test -p athena-core
demonstrations.observes: A: Failed with the environment reason, no producer call, the blocker in the note and the outcome. B: the producer ran and the note lists each probed tool as present, recorded in the dispatch commit. C: the preflight stop keeps the earlier job's kept work, names the earlier job, and the attempt is not flagged resumed.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the hook in `dispatch` is removed or runs after the producer, A fails: the producer runs and the job does not end with the environment reason. If `Job.note` is not set, A and B fail on the note assertions. If the context keeps `resume` on a blocked job, C fails because `remove_kept_work` removes the kept directory (close.rs:152-154). If `resumed_candidate` is not fixed, C fails on `resumed == false`.

demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test lifecycle baseline_failure_does_not_stop_the_job && cargo test -p athena-core preflight_records_every_probed_tool && cargo test -p athena-core preflight_skips && cargo test -p athena-core preflight_gh_is_not_a_need
